name: Per-task AI savings for software estimates
basis: Leanware's planning figures for a senior team that uses agentic coding tools (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot) every day, derived from a review of published studies dated to 2026-10-28. Every percentage is an inference, not a measured result; typical teams in the studies save less. 'aggressive' is the saving applied when an item is easy to hand to AI; 'floor' is where it falls when it is not (the conservative column of the research). 'expected_reference' is the research's middle column, kept for reference and not applied.
formula: D = weighted attribute score / (2 x sum of weights) = weighted sum / 30; saving = floor + (aggressive - floor) x D; then gates; never above aggressive; never below min(0, floor).

activities.label: Project setup, scaffolding and CI/CD bootstrap
activities.what_ai_does_not_save: Stack and repo-layout decisions, house conventions, cloud accounts and secrets, approving the production pipeline

activities.label: CRUD screens and standard business logic
activities.what_ai_does_not_save: Settling ambiguous business rules and edge cases, permission and data-integrity decisions, client acceptance

activities.label: UI built from an existing design system
activities.what_ai_does_not_save: Visual QA across browsers and screen sizes, accessibility review, interaction polish, fidelity to design intent

activities.label: Integrations with documented APIs
activities.what_ai_does_not_save: Sandbox and credential access, auth flows, webhook ordering and idempotency, vendor quirks, reconciliation edge cases

activities.label: Integrations with legacy or undocumented systems
activities.what_ai_does_not_save: Discovering undocumented behavior, test-environment access, knowledge held by client staff, side effects on systems of record

activities.label: Data modeling and database migrations
activities.what_ai_does_not_save: Normalization, tenancy and ownership decisions, backfill and rollback strategy, live-data safety

activities.label: AI features (retrieval, prompts, evaluations, guardrails)
activities.what_ai_does_not_save: Defining success criteria, reading real outputs, labeling, re-running evaluations on every model or prompt change, safety sign-off

activities.label: Debugging and bug fixing
activities.what_ai_does_not_save: Reproducing the bug, production access and logs, root-cause judgment across systems, proving no regression

activities.label: Refactoring and large mechanical migrations
activities.what_ai_does_not_save: Choosing the target design, building the validation harness, the long tail of edge cases, rollout and equivalence sign-off

activities.label: Automated test generation and test automation
activities.what_ai_does_not_save: Deciding which behavior matters and what correct looks like, flaky-test triage, test data and environments, owning the suite

activities.label: Manual and exploratory QA
activities.what_ai_does_not_save: Noticing what feels wrong, usability, unspecified behavior, go or no-go decisions, checking AI-written test cases are real

activities.label: Code documentation and technical writing
activities.what_ai_does_not_save: Deciding what to document and for whom, rationale that is not in the code, factual accuracy, editorial review

activities.label: Code review
activities.what_ai_does_not_save: Judging design fit and whether the change should exist, business context, approval accountability; AI produces more and larger changes to review

activities.label: Security and compliance
activities.what_ai_does_not_save: Risk judgment, proving a patch keeps behavior intact, attack chains in business logic, security review of AI-written code, attestation

activities.label: DevOps and infrastructure
activities.what_ai_does_not_save: Network and permission design, production change approval and rollback, environment failures outside the model's view

activities.label: UI/UX design
activities.what_ai_does_not_save: Research with real users, design judgment, production visual polish, design review

activities.label: Requirements and discovery
activities.what_ai_does_not_save: Getting the truth from real stakeholders, prioritization trade-offs, sign-off

activities.label: Business domain understanding
activities.what_ai_does_not_save: Unwritten rules, exceptions and politics, why a process exists, who actually decides

activities.label: Delivery and project management
activities.what_ai_does_not_save: Coordination and unblocking, sequencing and escalation decisions, risk judgment

activities.label: Client communication and stakeholder management
activities.what_ai_does_not_save: Live conversations, scope and price negotiation, expectation-setting, trust

attributes.label: Verifiability
attributes.two: An automated pass/fail check exists (tests, compiler, type checker, terraform plan, screenshot vs mockup) and checking costs far less than creating
attributes.one: Partial check; behaviour still needs human review
attributes.zero: Correctness is a human judgment (taste, intent, UX, architecture, client agreement)

attributes.label: Specification clarity
attributes.two: Written acceptance criteria, design or API contract; done is defined

attributes.label: Tacit knowledge
attributes.two: Everything needed is in the repo, docs or prompt
attributes.one: Some unwritten conventions that one person can write down in under an hour
attributes.zero: Depends on rules, history or processes that live in people's heads

attributes.label: Codebase state and familiarity
attributes.two: Greenfield, or a small, loosely coupled module
attributes.zero: Large, mature, tightly coupled brownfield, or the assigned engineer already maintains this exact code quickly

attributes.label: Complexity and novelty
attributes.two: Boilerplate, CRUD, standard patterns, docs, tests of clear behaviour
attributes.zero: Novel algorithms, concurrency, performance tuning, cross-cutting design

attributes.label: Context size
attributes.two: A few files; fits easily in one session
attributes.one: Tens of files or several services
attributes.zero: Many repos or services, or very large schemas

attributes.label: Language and API popularity
attributes.two: Mainstream language, framework and high-frequency APIs (TypeScript, Python, Java, React, Postgres, Stripe)
attributes.one: Less common framework or documented internal libraries
attributes.zero: Niche or legacy language, proprietary DSL, low-frequency or undocumented API

attributes.label: Task length vs model reliability
attributes.two: Splits into verifiable steps, each within the current 80%-reliability horizon (H80)
attributes.zero: Cannot be cut into checkable steps

attributes.label: Stakes and reversibility
attributes.one: Production, reversible behind flags or rollback
attributes.zero: Auth, payments, PII, compliance, irreversible data or infrastructure operations

gates.rule: stakes = 0 (authentication, payments, personal data, compliance, irreversible operations)
gates.effect: minus 5 points; minus 10 if the agent writes the security-sensitive code

gates.rule: unfamiliar codebase with no agent-ready docs or test commands (cold start)
gates.effect: minus 5 points, or price one context-setup item per codebase instead (0.5 to 2 days)

gates.rule: expected AI diff far larger than a human diff and not sliced

gates.effect: never below 0%; flagged as a slowdown risk when D < 0.25. Only code review, whose floor is negative, can go below 0%

downstream_reserve.rule: add back lambda x hours saved on code-producing rows, for the review, QA, security and stability load AI output creates downstream; lambda 0.10, or 0.20 when the estimate has no code-review or QA lines

review_and_qa_rule: Code review and QA are priced on the hours the build would take without AI (never shrunk in proportion to the AI-reduced build), then get their own rows.

h80.note: Score the task-length attribute against the applied value (lower end of the October 2026 extrapolation from METR's time-horizon data, about a four-month doubling). Replace with the newest published METR measurement at every re-date.

default_splits_note: Defaults used when a work item gives no split for its derived QA, delivery or design days. They are working defaults, not research figures; override them per item when the work is clearly one kind.
